questions.q: What is Ferriss’s main rule for approaching health?
a: Keep it simple and stick to a few rules of thumb
Track every possible biomarker daily
Follow the most detailed plan available
Change your routine every few weeks
questions.why: Lesson 1 says rules of thumb you actually use beat exact details you never apply.

questions.q: Which rule belongs to the Slow-Carb Diet?
a: Take one cheat day a week
Eat fruit with every meal
Drink milk with your coffee
Skip breakfast most mornings
questions.why: Lesson 1 lists five rules, including no fruit and one weekly day of unrestricted eating.

questions.q: What does the summary say about tracking data, even without changing anything?
a: Awareness alone tends to shift your behaviour
It only works if you count calories
It needs professional supervision to help
It has no effect until you set a goal
questions.why: Lesson 2 quotes the idea that what gets measured gets managed, through sheer awareness.

questions.q: Which simple measure does the summary suggest tracking?
a: Total inches across arms, legs, hips and waist
Your resting heart rate every morning
The number of steps you take weekly
Your body-fat percentage each day
questions.why: Lesson 2 offers one combined number for several body measurements, plus weekly weight and photos.

A reward you give yourself after progress
A setback that makes you start over
A routine you follow without thinking
questions.why: Lesson 3 says such a moment is what fuels real commitment to changing your health.
